targets.authors: Bryk, A. S., & Raudenbush, S. W.
targets.title: Toward a More Appropriate Conceptualization of Research on School Effects: A Three-Level Hierarchical Linear Model.
targets.evidence_quote: Our results replicate both the original Coleman Report ICCs, as well as those from Bryk and Raudenbush’s study.
targets.outcome_quote: Our results replicate both the original Coleman Report ICCs, as well as those from Bryk and Raudenbush’s study. In the left column of Table 1 (variation in achievement levels), our results are largely consistent with the Coleman Report: Only 23.7% of the variance in math achievement levels lies between schools (21.4% in ELA). When it comes to linear growth rates (middle panel of Table 1), our results are quite similar to the surprising findings from Bryk and Raudenbush: The majority—73.5%—of the variance in math learning rates lies between schools (80.7% in ELA).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall replication verdict covers both target studies, supported by target-specific comparisons. Scaling sensitivity and cautious interpretation do not negate the stated successful replication.
